articles: pointer-capture-board
Keep touch drags working beyond a puzzle board edge
Input
A selected tile may stop following a finger once the pointer crosses the element boundary, causing inconsistent drops and frustration.
Capture the pointer on pointerdown and track its pointerId, including pointerup and pointercancel. Release capture explicitly and clear dragging state on visibility loss.
Begin a move inside cell B3, drag outside the board, then return and release. The interface should still know which piece is active.
Touch scrolling or an incoming call can generate pointercancel. Test cancellation without ghost dragging and ensure ordinary page scroll remains available.
PTR,WCAG
keyboard-parity-puzzles
Make every essential puzzle action reachable by keyboard
Input
A swipe-only mechanic excludes players who cannot or do not use touch gestures. Keyboard interaction needs a visible, systematic alternative.
Use focusable tile buttons, arrow key movement where appropriate, and Enter or Space to rotate. Keep reset, hint and next controls in natural Tab order.
Complete one entire mirror puzzle without a pointing device; track whether the active tile retains focus after rotation and after a win.
A document-level handler that intercepts every arrow and Tab key can break navigation. Scope controls to the game region and test screen readers.
WCAG,PTR
two-tap-drag-fallback
Offer a two-tap alternative to complex dragging
Input
Dragging between distant grid cells requires motor precision and may conflict with touch scrolling. A simple select-then-target mode can make the same game playable.
Allow a tap to select a source piece and a second tap to select its destination. Show a clear selection outline and permit Escape or Cancel.
Moving a tile from A2 to D2 should obey exactly the same collision and movement rules whether performed by drag or two-tap selection.
If tapping already inspects a tile, explain when the interface is in move mode. Avoid overlapping gestures with ambiguous outcomes.
WCAG,PTR
focus-return-menus
Return keyboard focus predictably after closing a menu
Input
After a level-complete overlay closes, the previous focused tile may no longer exist, leaving keyboard users stranded.
Focus a relevant heading or primary button when the dialog opens, and restore focus to the invoking control when it closes. Keep focus within a truly modal dialog.
Press Enter to finish a stage, use Next, then reach the first interactive tile without touching the mouse or cycling through irrelevant page links.
Hidden overlays should not retain focusable elements. Test with a screen reader, keyboard-only input and repeated open-close cycles.
WCAG,LIVE
touch-controls-spacing
Design reachable action buttons for narrow mobile screens
Input
Hint, Pause and Restart are often grouped into tiny icons that fingers cannot operate reliably. Wrong taps may erase progress.
Increase actual hit target area, maintain visible spacing, and separate destructive controls from high-frequency actions. Test at 360 CSS pixels wide.
A 20-pixel icon can sit inside a roughly 44-pixel interactive region. Verify that adjacent button hitboxes do not overlap.
Invisible hit areas can still create accidental activations. Perform repeated one-handed play tests and check focus outlines.
WCAG,PTR
pause-on-visibility
Freeze game time when the browser becomes hidden
Input
A timed stage may expire while the user answers a call or switches apps, punishing unavoidable interruptions.
Use visibilitychange to freeze simulation time, hold remaining countdown and resume on an explicit user action. Record state in memory before the page hides.
If a player had 18 seconds remaining, returning after a minute should not create a huge physics time step or instantly end the round.
Discarding elapsed time without resetting the frame clock can still move objects abruptly. Test app switching, screen locking and landscape rotation.
PTR,STORE
fixed-step-physics
Use stable simulation steps across different refresh rates
Input
A game that advances one fixed distance each animation frame behaves differently at 60 Hz and 120 Hz and becomes unfair across devices.
Accumulate elapsed real time and advance physics in bounded fixed steps; render separately with requestAnimationFrame. Cap catch-up work after a hidden-tab interval.
At 60 simulation steps per second, each step represents about 16.67 milliseconds, regardless of whether the display requests 60 or 144 redraws.
Do not run an unlimited catch-up loop after a ten-minute pause. Replay a seeded input recording across refresh rates and compare final state.
CAN,INP
input-response-traces
Measure action responsiveness independently of display refresh
Input
A high-refresh display is not a substitute for responsive event callbacks when the JavaScript main thread is blocked.
Measure pointer timestamps, callback duration and visible presentation in a browser trace. Compare idle performance with animation and third-party scripts enabled.
A 100-millisecond long task can delay an action even when the screen refreshes every seven milliseconds. Remove the block before increasing decorative animation.
Do not convert number of animation frames directly into milliseconds. Report measured distributions for the tested hardware.
INP,PTR
scroll-versus-tap
Distinguish intentional card taps from touch scrolling
Input
A gallery card may navigate when a user tries to swipe the page, especially if pointerdown immediately triggers a game launch.
Wait for a valid click activation or use a measured drag threshold; handle pointercancel and retain normal anchor behavior for navigation.
Swipe vertically across a large game tile and confirm the catalog scrolls without opening the game. A stationary short tap should still activate it.
Preventing all touch defaults can break page scroll and pinch zoom. Test slow scroll, fast scroll and stylus input.
PTR,WCAG
accessible-action-feedback
Give one clear response for each shield or undo action
Input
Players repeat an action when the interface delays acknowledgement, potentially spending two shields for one intention.
Update the visible button state immediately, make only one state transition per activation and announce major changes in a polite live region.
When the shield count drops from 2 to 1, both visual and accessible feedback should reflect the new value before the next independent action.
Announcing every animation frame overwhelms assistive technology. Test rapid taps, key repeats and one-to-one action event handling.
LIVE,INP
